title: A rapid analysis of Bisphenol A using MISPE coupled with HPLC-FLD in tissues of food-producing animals
author: Cerkvenik-Flajs, Šturm
materials: A 50 µl aliquot of the final sample extract was taken for the HPLC analysis. A Hypersil GOLD C18 (150 × 4.6 mm, 3 μm particle size) analytical column was used which was protected by a Hypersil GOLD 3μ drop in guard cartridges (Thermo Scientific, Waltham, MA, USA). The chromatographic process was performed at room temperature (25‒26 °C), while the mobile phase as a mixture of H2O (constituent A) and MeCN (constituent B) was pumped at a flow rate of 1.0 ml/min and the excitation and emission wavelengths of the fluorescence spectrometric detection were set at 230 and 315 nm, respectively [21]. For muscle tissue and kidney analysis, the mobile phase constituents were gradient pumped in the following volume ratios: time 0–2 min (35% B), time 2–12 min (gradient 35–50% B), time 12–20 min (50% B), time 20–20.5 min (gradient 50–35% B), time 20.5–21 min (35% B) [21]. For liver analysis, the last gradient ramp (50–35% B) was prolonged from 20–25 min, and thus the whole chromatographic run time for this matrix was 25.5 min. BPA sample concentrations were calculated according to the external standard calibration.

steps.title: Weigh and extract tissue
steps.instruction: Weigh 2.0 ± 0.005 g of homogenised (defrosted) tissue into a 15 ml polypropylene centrifuge tube, add 8 ml acetonitrile (MeCN), vortex for 2 min, ultrasonicate for 13 min, then vibromix for 1 min.

steps.title: Centrifuge and re‑extract
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the tube at room temperature for 10 min at 2640 × g, decant the supernatant, add a further 2 ml MeCN, repeat vortex/ultrasonication if desired, combine the supernatants.

steps.title: Evaporate to aqueous residue
steps.instruction: Evaporate the combined supernatants under a nitrogen stream at 40 °C until only an aqueous residue remains.

steps.title: Re‑dissolve residue (original method)
steps.instruction: Dissolve the residue in 0.3 ml methanol (MeOH) and 4.7 ml water (H₂O) before loading onto the SPE cartridge (original method only).

steps.title: Re‑dissolve residue (present method)
steps.instruction: Dissolve the residue in 1 ml MeCN and 10 ml H₂O before loading onto the MISPE cartridge (present method only).

steps.title: SPE – original two‑cartridge workflow
steps.instruction: Perform the original Deceuninck et al. SPE sequence using a Chromabond HR‑X cartridge followed by a MISPE BPA cartridge.

substeps.instruction: Condition HR‑X cartridge with 10 ml MeOH then 10 ml H₂O (gravity).
Load the re‑dissolved extract onto the HR‑X cartridge (gravity).
Wash HR‑X sequentially with 6 ml H₂O, 8 ml MeOH/H₂O (10/90, v/v), and 4 ml MeOH/H₂O (60/40, v/v).
Elute HR‑X with 10 ml MeOH into a 15 ml glass centrifuge tube; evaporate under N₂ at 40 °C to dryness.
Re‑dissolve the eluate in 0.2 ml MeCN and 5 ml H₂O.
Condition the MISPE BPA cartridge with 10 ml MeOH/HCOOH (98/2, v/v), 4 ml MeCN, and 4 ml H₂O (gravity).
Load the re‑dissolved HR‑X eluate onto the MISPE cartridge (gravity).
Wash MISPE with 5 ml H₂O, then 3 ml MeCN/H₂O (40/60, v/v), then 3 ml MeCN.
Elute BPA with 4 ml MeOH (modified from original 6 ml) into a 15 ml glass tube; evaporate under N₂ at 40 °C to dryness.
Re‑dissolve the final eluate in 0.8 ml MeCN/H₂O (35/65, v/v), ultrasonicate 5 min, vibromix, centrifuge 10 min at 2640 × g, and transfer to an HPLC vial.

steps.title: SPE – present single‑cartridge workflow
steps.instruction: Perform the optimized MISPE‑only procedure on the same tissue extract.

substeps.instruction: Condition the MISPE BPA cartridge with 10 ml MeOH/HCOOH (98/2, v/v), 4 ml MeCN, and 4 ml H₂O (gravity).
Load the re‑dissolved extract (1 ml MeCN + 10 ml H₂O) onto the cartridge (gravity).
Wash with 5 ml H₂O followed by 3 ml MeCN/H₂O (40/60, v/v).
Elute BPA with 6 ml MeOH into a 15 ml glass centrifuge tube; evaporate under N₂ at 40 °C to dryness.
Re‑dissolve the dried eluate in 0.8 ml MeCN/H₂O (35/65, v/v), ultrasonicate 5 min, vibromix, centrifuge 10 min at 2640 × g, and transfer to an HPLC vial.

steps.title: HPLC‑FLD analysis
steps.instruction: Inject 50 µl of the final extract onto a Hypersil GOLD C18 column (150 × 4.6 mm, 3 µm) equipped with a guard cartridge; run at 25‑26 °C with a flow of 1.0 ml/min; detect fluorescence at excitation 230 nm and emission 315 nm.

substeps.instruction: For muscle and kidney: gradient – 0‑2 min 35 % B, 2‑12 min linear to 50 % B, 12‑20 min hold 50 % B, 20‑20.5 min linear back to 35 % B, 20.5‑21 min hold 35 % B.
For liver: same as above but extend the 50‑to‑35 % B ramp from 20‑25 min, giving a total run time of 25.5 min.
